\paragraph{Limitations of $\aeff$ as a proxy.}
The $\aeff$ diagnostic correlates with the true batch-level real fraction at Pearson $r \approx 0.79$ (${\sim}$63\% of variance; Appendix~\ref{app:alpha_validation}), stable across seeds (Spearman $\rho_s \geq 0.86$; Table~\ref{tab:alpha_corr_perseed}).
The ceiling is set by detector calibration, not batch size: scaling to $B{=}16$ leaves $R^2$ in the 0.59--0.63 range, though the adaptive advantage still increases monotonically ($1.0{\times}$ to $3.0{\times}$; \S\ref{sec:sensitivity}).
Because the convergence guarantee of \citet{wang2026survive} requires the \emph{true} real fraction, the ${\sim}$37\% unexplained variance means some batches satisfying $\aeff \geq \tau$ may have true fractions below $\tau$; the $\nmin$ constraint mitigates this by capping $b$ at the ESS floor, preventing weight concentration where the proxy is unreliable~\citep{owen2013mc}.
